what: the corpus lane's resting call for every row of the translation tables at the places of the Targum and the Zohar (relay v221): a row names a spelling and no place, and where a dictionary the lane holds lists the spelling as two or more words, the lane says, place by place, whether the text's word there is the row's word or another word written alike. Kept here byte for byte in the folder the lane keeps it in, with its rule, its answer, its receipt and second count, the known misfires, the two rows' verdicts and the strike list. tools/apply-held-places-v1.mjs writes, on the word of each place the list marks held at rest, the rows held there and the line the place reads without them; the reader withholds those rows from the word's card there under «only this pointing», and they stand at every other place

held_at_rest.says: the lane's resting call (RULE.md, Amended 10): HELD_BY_CITATION, HELD_BY_POINTS and HELD_BY_CORPUS_ENTRY_WORD hold at rest; every other class stands

keyed_by.says: a place is found on our zone by its row (m, key and words), its work and its verse unit, and carries its class; the lane's token row is its own edition's and is never read here (the letter, section 4: our commentary text may be another edition)

branches_off_at_rest.says: labelled on the places they would hold (branches) and off at rest; turning one on is the lane's call, so nothing is held by them
